title: ase.parallel: Do not create communicator too early
body:
I want to detect whenever we fail to control how communicators are passed in different places.  Often someone forgets to set a communicator and it defaults to world.  That likely causes a nasty deadlock when the caller tries to do processing on a different communicator.

So we want to monkeypatch the world communicator so it is 'broken', so we get a crash instead of a deadlock.

In order to 'break' it (by monkeypatching, e.g. from inside test suite) we need to mutate it, and that is impossible on GPAW's C communicator: Both the instance and its type are completely immutable.  So we need to import the Python wrapper (which we can monkeypatch), and we need to be not-too-eager about it in order not to get a crash due to cyclic import.  Hence this change.

Although this could probably be achieved in nicer ways, the communicator import order is a bit of a minefield.
